blocks: apps/api/tests/unit/approvalWorkflowUseCases.test.ts::creates a workflow with description and isDefault
subject: packages/core/approvals/src/CreateApprovalWorkflowUseCase.ts
note: The ledger row has no subject; the block's title names CreateApprovalWorkflowUseCase, which the test imports from @core/approvals. The block's verdict, that a default workflow is created for an account with no default yet, comes from its default branch, which inverts its check of the current default, so it reads the fields of a missing workflow and the creation fails.

subject: apps/api/src/audit/auditService.ts
note: The block's verdict, that a resource-id filter finds the log of that resource, comes from the where clause AuditService.getLogs builds. The clause writes the resource id into the resource key, so no log matches. A first mutation, the resource-id filter dropped, read VACUOUS: the seed holds one Post log, so the block found it with or without the filter.

subject: apps/api/src/audit/auditService.ts
note: The block's verdict, that every top resource carries a resource name, comes from the top-resources mapping of AuditService.getStats. The mapping reads each group's resource id in place of its resource, so the names are undefined. A first mutation, the aggregation's exclusion of logs with no resource dropped, read VACUOUS: the test's groupBy double skips empty keys itself and the seed holds no log without a resource.

subject: apps/api/src/audit/auditService.ts
note: The block's verdict, that the top users come in descending order of their log count, comes from the top-users aggregation of AuditService.getStats. The aggregation orders its groups by user id. A first mutation, the count order turned ascending, read VACUOUS too: the test's groupBy double sorts its groups by descending count whatever orderBy it receives, so the block pinned the double's own sort, and no reader of the service's orderBy exists without a double that applies it or a test against Postgres.

subject: apps/api/src/posts/optimizedPostsRoutes.ts
